title: How this assistant is set up
snapshot: A snapshot, not a live feed. Nothing on a timer publishes this page.
lede: What this practice has, why it is built this way, and what someone else would get. Written for a person, not for the machine.
footer: Unified Solutions. This page describes a system. It does not coach, and it does not hold client work.
have_intro: Four choices hold the design. Each one is here because the other way leaks something.

tiles.title: You talk
tiles.text: The assistant meets you where you already talk. You still decide.

tiles.title: It remembers
tiles.text: How you work stays on this computer. It does not copy every sentence.

tiles.title: Minds stay separate
tiles.text: A gift is another mind. It is not a second login on this one.

tiles.title: Private stays here
tiles.text: Session talk and client files do not go to a cloud model.

skills_intro: These are the kinds of work, not the internal names of the tools. A person should not have to learn the machine to see the fence.
can: Talk with you, and answer in speech.
Draft an email, a post, a page, a deck, or a sheet. You send it.
Look at the calendar and help find a time.
Read a file you name. The read stays on this machine.
Remember how you like the work done, on purpose, on this computer.
Keep the backup, the morning look, and the weekly review you already asked for.
Tell you when something you already run is stuck.
cannot: Send the email, post the page, or pay a bill on its own.
Sit in a coaching session, or replace your judgment.
Open a client file because it appeared on a calendar.
Store a client name, a session note, or a document in the memory that stays on this computer.
Share this mind, these keys, or these files with someone else.
Promise that a cloud company keeps nothing. That has not been confirmed.
Use a model hosted in China for names, scheduling, or private talk.
setup_intro: One mind for this practice. A second profile on the same install is the pattern not to copy. A gift is a separate login.

setup.title: This practice
setup.why: One install, one set of rules, one mouth. You talk to it in Slack. The desktop is the same assistant.
points: It can use files, calendar, and email on this machine. Those tools are fenced.
A client document stays closed until you name the file.

setup.title: Do not copy this
setup.why: A second profile on this same install shares the computer user and the model login. That is not a gift.
points: Do not hand this pattern to another person.

setup.title: A gifted mind
setup.why: Separate login, separate home, separate keys. Same computer today. Not the same mind.
points: The graphics card is not shared.
Their name, talk, and keys are not on this page.

folders_intro: Work is sorted by the kind of work, not by a business name. The assistant's own files sit apart from the practice.

folders.title: Practice work
folders.why: One folder. Strategy, operations, finance, communications, research, data. Not one folder per venture.

folders.title: The assistant
folders.why: Settings, memory, sessions, and keys live apart from the business files. They are not filed with the work.

folders.title: A gifted person's files
folders.why: Their own folder. This snapshot did not open it. Side notes have leaked into the practice folders. Do not describe that as a second house.

folders.title: The public site
folders.why: Its own place. Shipped apart from drafts. This page is not the practice site.

security_intro: The fence is a rule the operator keeps. It is not a locked room that makes a mistake impossible.

security.title: Separate minds
security.why: A gift does not get this login, these keys, or these files. A steward can see whether it is up. Not what was said.

security.title: Words leave on purpose
security.why: Ordinary work can go to a US cloud model. Private talk and client files stay on this computer, on a small local model.

security.title: A named file is not a standing key
security.why: Seeing a file is not permission to open it. If you name one, the read stays here. The next file is still closed.

security.title: Memory is local and on purpose
security.why: It remembers how the work is done. It does not vacuum every sentence. It does not hold client names. The online search for that memory is off.

security.title: This page is a fence too
security.why: Names, keys, and other people's talk are not published here. If a fact is missing, that is the point.

security.title: A model in China is not a backup
security.why: It is used by hand, and only on text that is already public. It does not get names or private talk.

gift.intro: You do not learn a terminal. You talk. Someone else keeps the computer on. You keep the decisions.

required.title: You talk, and you name it
required.text: Day one is a conversation. You decide what to call it. You do not inherit this personality.

required.title: A phone you already text from
required.text: You text first. Until you do, it cannot start the conversation.

required.title: A folder for your files
required.text: Your files are not this practice's files. Drop what you want it to know. It does not browse the rest.

required.title: Someone keeps the computer on
required.text: They pay for the model and can see whether it is up. They do not read the talk. You do not use their login.

required.title: You decide what can leave
required.text: Public work can go out. Private talk stays. You do not edit a settings file to say so.

easy: Drafts come back to you. You send them.
You do not open this computer, this Slack, or a settings screen.
If it is down, the person who runs it can see that. They cannot read what you said.
not: This login, these keys, this graphics card, or these practice files.
A second profile on this install. That is the pattern to avoid.

operator.intro: The detail sits here so the person who runs it can check the snapshot. A guest does not need it to understand the brief.

facts.label: Everyday brain
facts.value: grok-4.7 via xai-oauth. Ordinary work leaves the machine.

facts.label: Private path
facts.value: A small open model on this computer. Private text stays here. It is not the most capable path.

facts.label: Speech
facts.value: What you say is transcribed here. A spoken reply sends those words to a speech service.

facts.label: Search
facts.value: A question can go to the US vendor. Reading a public page starts here.

facts.label: Scheduled work
facts.value: 32 running, 3 paused, 35 in all. Job names are not on this page.

notes: The morning look, the weekly review, and the nightly backup keep running. A daily cost note is paused on purpose.
The private path fits a 10 GB card. It keeps text home. It is not a frontier model.
Session history on this install is large. Compacting it waits until the gateway is stopped. It is not done.
A software update is waiting. It was not applied for this snapshot.

limits.title: The backup path matches the written rule
limits.detail: At this snapshot, the extra stop was not on the parent chain. Ordinary failure goes to a US model, then to the small model on this computer.

limits.title: Do not claim the vendor keeps nothing
limits.detail: By rule, session content does not go to a cloud model. Zero-retention on the cloud account has not been confirmed. The rule is not a vendor promise.

limits.title: Privacy is a rule, not a sealed room
limits.detail: There is no locked profile that makes a cloud call impossible. Disk encryption is still an open item. Say that before calling the machine a vault.

limits.title: Folders do not separate the ventures
limits.detail: The house sorts by kind of work. Side efforts have leaked into those folders. Do not describe this as one folder per business.

limits.title: The gift shares the computer, not the keys
limits.detail: Isolation here is a separate login, a separate home, and separate keys. It is not a separate machine. The original bar was a separate host. Last check: up.

not_on_this_page: Client names, session content, and client files.
Other people's names, conversations, phone numbers, and files.
The private cockpit used day to day.
